questions.description: Microsoft Learn unit: Describe Azure virtual networking
questions.question: Which statement best describes Azure Virtual Network (VNet)?

options.text: An encrypted tunnel that carries trusted private-network traffic across an untrusted network such as the internet
The default resiliency configuration in which a standby VPN gateway instance can take over during failure

questions.description: Microsoft Learn unit: Describe Azure virtual networking
questions.question: Select the TWO statements that are correct according to this unit.

options.text: Azure Virtual Network (VNet): an endpoint with a private IP address inside a virtual network.
Azure Virtual Network (VNet): a private network in Azure that enables resources to communicate securely with each other and with external networks.
Public endpoint: an encrypted tunnel that carries trusted private-network traffic across an untrusted network such as the internet.
Subnet: a subdivision of a virtual network address space used to segment resources.
Subnet: a private connection between VNets that uses the Microsoft backbone instead of the public internet.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Azure Virtual Network (VNet) — a private network in Azure that enables resources to communicate securely with each other and with external networks; and Subnet — a subdivision of a virtual network address space used to segment resources.

Public endpoint: an endpoint with a public IP address that can be reachable from the internet.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Public endpoint — an endpoint with a public IP address that can be reachable from the internet; and Private endpoint — an endpoint with a private IP address inside a virtual network.

questions.question: Select TWO correct statements about the material in this Microsoft Learn unit.

Network security group (NSG): a resource containing inbound and outbound rules that allow or deny network traffic.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Network security group (NSG) — a resource containing inbound and outbound rules that allow or deny network traffic; and User-defined route (UDR) — a custom route used to control traffic flow between subnets or virtual networks.
